retired: deleted by phase-426 W4; the row records the reasoning that retired it
why: RETIRED 2026-09-11 (phase-426 W4, second half): `nros::ParameterServer<Capacity, SeqSlots, SeqPoolBytes>` IS DELETED. What follows is the reasoning that produced the row and then retired it; the class no longer exists, so nothing here is a claim about today's surface. It was a fixed-capacity, node-local typed parameter store, storage inline, no heap, over the LEGACY caller-storage C `nros_parameter_server_t` -- which means its parameters were NOT what `ros2 param` sees: the six `rcl_interfaces/srv/*` servers read a DIFFERENT object, the `nros_params::ParameterServer` the executor owns, and nothing joined them. rclcpp has no such type because rclcpp's parameters live ON the node and the node allocates. THREE FACTS DECIDED THE RETIREMENT, all measured. (1) NO CONSUMER. After the first half of W4 deleted both node-owned C++ stores, `grep -rn 'ParameterServer<' packages examples book docs` found the class constructed in exactly one place in the tree: `examples/linux/cpp/parameters`, the example that documented it. A caller-owned store with no executor is a capability we had no caller for. (2) IT WAS THE DEFECT, SHIPPED. An example is COPIED OUT (RFC-0026), so the shipped answer to "how do I use parameters in C++" was the store `ros2 param get` cannot read -- which is the whole of what phase-426 exists to remove. (3) IT IS WRAPPER-SIDE BEHAVIOUR. RFC-0019/0020 and RFC-0089 §"Parameters" put storage, typing, the read-only and range rules and the node keying in Rust and leave the C++ API a call-shape adapter; a ~600-line header with a name table and a bump-allocated element pool is the second implementation that rule forbids. Disposition is ABSENT (RFC-0089's fourth), which is available here because upstream never had the name -- the alias rule only binds where rclcpp HAS a name and we lack it. The capability moved rather than went: `nros::Seq<T, N>` survives as a VALUE (see `cpp:Seq`) and now declares and reads through the node API onto the executor's store, so a freestanding sequence parameter is visible to `ros2 param get` for the first time -- measured 2026-09-11, `ros2 param get /cpp_parameters mpc_weights` -> `array('d', [4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0])`. The `raw()` accessor went with the class and nothing mourned it: it was documented for "C-API helpers (e.g. ROS 2 service registration)" that do not exist -- `rclc_parameter_server_init_default` takes the node, never a standalone store. The C family it wrapped still ships, as `rclc_parameter_*`; what changed is that no example demonstrates it (`check-example-parameter-stores`). Phase 379 W3, retired phase-426 W4.
